findings.note: ESPN's bio page lists Nichushkin as a Columbus Blue Jackets right wing with status 'OUT'. No reason or date is given, but it is a serious warning: he may not play, so check the lineup and the book's void rules before betting.

In 2026-27 he has 2 goals and 9 assists in 20 games for CBJ, about 17:19 TOI per game. He had an assist in 9 of 20 games, including 3 of his last 5 (through Nov 19 at CHI, 18:25 TOI). No later game appears in the log shown.

Analysis from the June 2026 trade says he was expected to be a second-line winger for Columbus. It also says he has averaged only 57 games a season over the past five years, which points to an ongoing injury and availability risk.

The NHL.com page shows 14 assists, 7 of them on the power play, and 23:53 average ice time in 24 games for Toronto. He had an assist in 4 of his last 5 games, through Nov 19. Contrary signs: Toronto lost all 6 games from Nov 3 to Nov 19, he is -10, and the page's date tag looks stale.

Rotowire's offseason note on CBS expected Raddysh to play on Toronto's top defensive pair and first power-play unit. None of the news shown is current game-week injury or lineup news for this game against the Islanders.
Background: Toronto got Raddysh from Tampa Bay in a sign-and-trade on an eight-year deal after his career-best 70-point (48-assist) season. This does not confirm that the scoring will carry over.

The Devils' preview says Werenski leads Columbus with 15 assists and has a four-game point streak (3G, 3A). It also lists Blue Jackets forwards Sean Monahan (upper body) and Conor Garland (IR) as injured, which could cut his assist chances. Devils defensemen Kovacevic and Casey are also out.

A Rotowire note from Nov 22 says Werenski had a goal and an assist against Toronto, his fourth straight game with a point (6 points). The same page lists Columbus as a heavy road underdog (NJ -206, total 6), which could limit his chances to get assists.

ESPN's team stats show Columbus scoring only 2.48 goals per game, which works against the bet. Working for it, New Jersey has a 64.2% penalty kill, and both of its listed goalies have save percentages below .900.

inputs.label: Projected ice time

inputs.label: Weighted assists / 60
inputs.detail: Prior-adjusted production per 60 minutes

inputs.label: Opponent goals allowed / game
inputs.detail: Recency-weighted; the same figure the game-line model uses

inputs.label: His results vs. our forecasts
inputs.detail: 129 actual vs. 118.3 forecast points in earlier games; shrunk toward 1

steps.label: Opponent goals allowed vs. long-run league average
His results vs. our past forecasts

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 129 points against 118.3 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.label: Production rate
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.label: Ice time
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: assists
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league.
